person.name: Franz_Kafka
person.summary: Franz Kafka (3 July 1883 – 3 June 1924) was a German-language Jewish Czech writer whose novels and stories, blending realism and the fantastique, explore themes of alienation, bureaucracy, and existential anxiety. Born in Prague, he trained and worked as a lawyer and insurance official while writing largely unpublished fiction that later became central to 20th‑century literature, including The Metamorphosis, The Trial, and The Castle.

events.title: Birth in Prague
events.description: Franz Kafka was born into a middle-class German- and Yiddish-speaking Jewish family near the Old Town Square in Prague, then part of the Kingdom of Bohemia in the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

images.caption: Plaque commemorating the birthplace of Franz Kafka in Prague.

location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.title: Attends German elementary school
events.description: From 1889 to 1893, Kafka attended the German boys' elementary school at the Masný trh/Fleischmarkt (now Masná Street), receiving his first formal education in German in Prague.

images.caption: Franz Kafka as a school pupil around 1899.

location_coordinates.label: Capital City of Prague, Prague, Czechia
location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.title: Studies at Altstädter Gymnasium
events.description: After elementary school, Kafka entered the rigorous, classics-oriented Altstädter Deutsches Gymnasium at Old Town Square in the Kinský Palace. Over eight years he studied in German, also taking Czech, and completed his secondary education there.

images.caption: The Kinský Palace on Prague's Old Town Square, where Kafka attended the Altstädter Deutsches Gymnasium.

location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.date_note: Kafka turned 13 in July 1896; bar mitzvah timing approximate within that year
events.title: Celebrates bar mitzvah
events.description: Kafka's Jewish education, which had included preparation for religious observance, effectively ended with his bar mitzvah celebration at the age of 13, after which he rarely attended synagogue except on major holidays.

location_coordinates.label: Capital City of Prague, Prague, Czechia
location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.title: Passes Matura examinations
events.description: Kafka completed his Matura examinations in 1901 at the Altstädter Deutsches Gymnasium, qualifying him for university study after eight years of classics-oriented secondary schooling.

location_coordinates.label: Capital City of Prague, Prague, Czechia
location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.title: Studies law in Prague
events.description: In 1901 Kafka enrolled at the Deutsche Karl-Ferdinands-Universität in Prague, initially for philosophy but switching to law after two weeks. Over five years he pursued legal studies, while also taking courses in German studies and art history and involving himself in literary student circles.

images.caption: Franz Kafka around 1906, the year he received his Doctor of Law degree.

location_coordinates.label: Capital City of Prague, Prague, Czechia
location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.title: Meets Max Brod
events.description: At the end of his first year at university, Kafka met fellow law student Max Brod, who became his closest lifelong friend and later the editor and preserver of his manuscripts. Their friendship formed the core of what Brod called the Close Prague Circle of German-speaking Jewish writers.

location_coordinates.label: Capital City of Prague, Prague, Czechia
location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.title: Earns Doctor of Law, clerks
events.description: Kafka was awarded the degree of Doctor of Law on 18 June 1906. He then completed a mandatory unpaid year as a law clerk in Prague's civil and criminal courts, gaining practical legal experience before entering full-time employment.

location_coordinates.label: Capital City of Prague, Prague, Czechia
location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.title: Works at Assicurazioni Generali
events.description: On 1 November 1907, Kafka began working at the Assicurazioni Generali insurance company in Prague. The long working hours left him little time to write and contributed to his dissatisfaction, leading to his resignation on 15 July 1908.

location_coordinates.label: Capital City of Prague, Prague, Czechia
location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.date_note: Kafka began at the institute two weeks after leaving Assicurazioni Generali in July 1908 and remained until he was pensioned in 1918 and increasingly ill in the early 1920s
events.title: Joins Workers' Accident Insurance Institute
events.description: Two weeks after leaving Assicurazioni Generali, Kafka joined the Workers' Accident Insurance Institute for the Kingdom of Bohemia in Prague. There he investigated industrial accidents, wrote reports and annual summaries, and advanced professionally while structuring his schedule to preserve time for writing.

images.caption: Former home of the Workers' Accident Insurance Institute in Prague, where Kafka worked as an insurance official.

location_coordinates.label: Capital City of Prague, Prague, Czechia
location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.title: Immerses in Yiddish theatre
events.description: After attending a Yiddish theatre troupe's performance in October 1911, Kafka spent about six months closely following Yiddish theatre in Prague, immersing himself in the Yiddish language and literature and deepening his engagement with Jewish culture.

location_coordinates.label: Capital City of Prague, Prague, Czechia
location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.title: Publishes Contemplation stories
events.description: In 1912 Kafka published the collection Contemplation (Betrachtung), a set of short prose pieces that was among the few works released during his lifetime and marked his emerging voice as a German-language modernist writer.

images.caption: Cover of Franz Kafka's 1912 collection Contemplation (Betrachtung).

events.title: Releases The Metamorphosis
events.description: Kafka's novella The Metamorphosis (Die Verwandlung) was published in 1915, telling the story of Gregor Samsa's sudden transformation into an insect and exemplifying Kafka's fusion of everyday realism with the fantastical and his themes of alienation and incomprehensible authority.

events.title: Diagnosed with tuberculosis
events.description: In 1917 Kafka was diagnosed with tuberculosis, a disease that increasingly interfered with his ability to work at the insurance institute and to write, eventually forcing him into periods of leave and contributing directly to his early death.

location_coordinates.label: Capital City of Prague, Prague, Czechia
location_coordinates.name: Prague

events.title: Dies of tuberculosis
events.description: Kafka died on 3 June 1924 from complications of tuberculosis, aged 40, after years of illness that had curtailed both his professional work and his literary production.
